items.title: 米特使2人が開戦後初めてキーウ入り、ロシアとの戦争終結に向け協議
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米国のスティーブ・ウィトコフ、ジャレッド・クシュナー両特使が、ウクライナ戦争勃発後で初めて、首都キーウを訪れた。ロシアがウクライナに全面侵攻してから4年半が経過した。米政府が再び進める和平のための取り組みが戦争終結につながるかについては、懐疑的な見方が根強い。

両特使は列車でキーウ入りし、市中心部にある歴史的な建造物である聖ソフィア大聖堂でゼレンスキー大統領の出迎えを受けた。ウクライナのウメロフ国家安全保障・国防会議書記は、両特使が列車から降りる様子を撮影した動画を投稿した。

ゼレンスキー氏は「広範囲にわたって十分に話し合う機会になるだろう」と発言。「トランプ米大統領が両氏の訪問を認めたことに感謝する」と述べた。ゼレンスキー氏によると、6日の協議には英国、ドイツ、フランス各国の当局者も参加する。

同氏はその後のXへの投稿で、予定されていた大聖堂の敷地内での協議が始まったことを明らかにした。

ウィトコフ氏とクシュナー氏は、5日にはモスクワでロシアのプーチン大統領と3時間余りにわたって会談した。ロシア大統領府の高官は「極めて有益」な会談だったと評価した。

会談の冒頭、プーチン氏は双方が解決すべき状況について「簡単なものではない」と述べた。ウクライナ政府の考えについて知る複数の関係者によれば、ウクライナ側は両特使の訪問で有意な進展が得られることについて悲観的にみている。

ゼレンスキー氏は両特使の到着を前に、ウメロフ氏を含む交渉チームを招集した。Xへの投稿でゼレンスキー氏は「われわれは協議の用意ができている。ウクライナはこれまでも、そして今後も建設的な姿勢を維持する」と表明。

「安全の保証が必要だ。戦後の和平は尊厳あるものでなければならない。われわれの提案は準備できている」と記した。

トランプ大統領は4日、両特使が「戦争終結に向けた提案を携えている」と述べたが、詳細には言及しなかった。トランプ氏は2025年の政権復帰に際し、この戦争は早期に終結させられると語っていたが、第2次世界大戦後の欧州で最も長期化したこの戦争は、終結への取り組みが難航している。

items.title: Son of EssilorLuxottica founder calls for new strategy for eyewear group
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Franco-Italian eyewear group EssilorLuxottica needs a new strategy after losing more than half of its stock market value in recent months, the son of its late founder said on Sunday.
items.body:
Franco-Italian eyewear group EssilorLuxottica (ESLX.PA) needs a new strategy after losing more than half of its stock market value in recent months, the son of its late founder said on Sunday.
Leonardo Maria Del Vecchio last month [USN:L8N44M08E TEXT:"stepped down"] from management roles at the group, whose brands include Ray-Ban, Oakley and Vogue Eyewear, after reported tensions with CEO Francesco Milleri, but remains an investor in the group through family holding company Delfin.
Speaking on the sidelines of the annual TEHA Ambrosetti conference on the shores of Lake Como, Del Vecchio said he was hoping for "a new chapter" for the group.
Delfin has a 32.4% stake in EssilorLuxottica and also owns stakes in several financial groups in Italy, including 17.5% of Monte dei Paschi (BMPS.MI) , which is the target of a [USN:L4N42G0DE TEXT:"takeover bid"] by Intesa Sanpaolo (ISP.MI) .
Del Vecchio said there was too much focus on his relations with Milleri, who also chairs Delfin, and the current consolidation wave in the Italian banking sector.
"Banks are a financial investment. The industrial investment that must be protected is EssilorLuxottica," Del Vecchio said. "EssilorLuxottica is Delfin's legacy, our father's true investment and enduring legacy, yet it has lost 50% of its market value."
Del Vecchio also said that no one had yet asked Delfin's investors what to do with the stake in Monte dei Paschi and criticised the board of the holding company for alleged opaqueness.

items.title: Népal Une vieille dame retrouvée vivante dans sa maison détruite
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Persuadée qu'elle avait trouvé la mort dans les inondations meurtrières du Népal, la famille de Chandika Kumari Shrestha avait entamé les rituels du deuil à sa mémoire.
items.body:
Persuadée qu'elle avait trouvé la mort dans les inondations meurtrières du Népal, la famille de Chandika Kumari Shrestha avait entamé les rituels du deuil à sa mémoire.
Dix jours plus tard, les sauveteurs ont retrouvée la vieille dame vivante à l'intérieur de sa maison effondrée dans le village de Betrawati, où elle a survécu dans l'eau et la boue grâce à une étroite poche d'air.
"La maison de quatre étages a été emportée par les inondations. En faisant un état des lieux, nous avons entendu une voix crier 'Au secours !' ", a raconté un officier de police, Mahendra Darnal. "J'étais en contact avec la famille et ils avaient entamé la période de deuil de 11 jours".
Dégagée samedi lors d'une opération de 45 minutes, la victime a été envoyée dans un hôpital militaire.
Des centaines de personnes sont portées disparues à Betrawati, une région du Népal parmi les plus durement touchées par les inondations, aujourd'hui recouverte d'une couche de boue blanche compacte dure comme du béton.
Les équipes de secours continuent de récupérer de nombreux corps.
Le marché de la ville et la plupart des immeubles d'habitation ont été ensevelis sous les débris charriés par le torrent qui a dévalé la vallée. La catastrophe due à l'effondrement d'un glacier a fait plus de 1.300 morts, et quelque 5.000 personnes sont toujours portées disparues.
Depuis vendredi, trois personnes ont été secourues, dont un ressortissant chinois, dans les tunnels où plus de 900 personnes ont été prises au piège.
D'autres, comme Chandika Kumari Shrestha, ont survécu dans des conditions extrêmes, notamment un garçon de huit ans qui a pu retrouver sa mère.

items.title: Los ataques israelíes causan cuatro muertos en el sur del Líbano
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Los ataques israelíes causaron la muerte de cuatro personas, entre ellas dos mujeres, en el sur del Líbano el domingo, según informó el Ministerio de Sanidad libanés, en lo que constituyó una represalia de Israel por lo que, según afirmó, fueron ataques con drones de Hezbolá en zonas ocupadas por sus tropas.
items.body:
Los ataques israelíes causaron la muerte de cuatro personas, entre ellas dos mujeres, en el sur del Líbano el domingo, según informó el Ministerio de Sanidad libanés, en lo que constituyó una represalia de Israel por lo que, según afirmó, fueron ataques con drones de Hezbolá en zonas ocupadas por sus tropas.
A pesar del alto el fuego con Hezbolá acordado en junio y negociado por Estados Unidos, el ejército israelí sigue operando en lo que ha declarado como zona de seguridad en el sur del Líbano.
El Ministerio de Sanidad libanés indicó que dos hombres murieron en una localidad situada en el límite de la zona ocupada por las tropas israelíes, mientras que las dos mujeres fallecieron en Arab Salim, que se encuentra bastante al norte de la zona ocupada.
El ejército israelí había emitido una advertencia de evacuación en línea a las 6:00 de la mañana, hora local (0300 GMT), para las zonas cercanas a un edificio en Arab Salim que, según afirmó, iba a atacar porque estaba siendo utilizado por Hezbolá. Dos niñas se encontraban entre las otras seis personas heridas en ese ataque.
La oficina del presidente libanés, Joseph Aoun, calificó los ataques del domingo —que, según afirmó, destruyeron un hospital y causaron daños en un edificio del Ministerio de Hacienda— de «una peligrosa escalada» dirigida contra "administraciones y centros sanitarios puramente civiles".
"El presidente Aoun responsabilizó plenamente a la parte israelí de esta escalada en curso y pidió a Estados Unidos y a la comunidad internacional que tomaran medidas inmediatas para detener estas violaciones y exigir responsabilidades a los autores", afirmó.
El ejército israelí afirmó que entre sus objetivos se encontraban lo que describió como instalaciones de almacenamiento de armas de Hezbolá y un centro de mando situado en el interior de un edificio que anteriormente se utilizaba como hospital. También señaló que utilizó munición de precisión y vigilancia aérea para minimizar los daños a la población civil.
La orden de evacuación del domingo fue solo la segunda emitida desde el anuncio del alto el fuego en junio.

items.title: En frontera China y Nepal, devastada por inundaciones, no queda rastro de un puerto: testigos Reuters
items.author: Nicoco Chan, Tingshu Wang
items.creator: Nicoco Chan, Tingshu Wang
items.summary: Unos 20 rescatistas chinos, vestidos de naranja brillante, utilizaron el domingo excavadoras, palas y detectores de radar en un intento por localizar a los cientos de personas desaparecidas desde que un deslizamiento de tierra, similar a un tsunami, arrasó el principal paso fronterizo de China con Nepal.
items.body:
Unos 20 rescatistas chinos, vestidos de naranja brillante, utilizaron el domingo excavadoras, palas y detectores de radar en un intento por localizar a los cientos de personas desaparecidas desde que un deslizamiento de tierra, similar a un tsunami, arrasó el principal paso fronterizo de China con Nepal.
El paso fronterizo de Gyirong, que separa el Tíbet chino de Nepal, se convirtió en un espeluznante símbolo de la devastación que siguió al derrumbe de un glaciar en el lado nepalí de la frontera el 26 de agosto.
Reuters y otras agencias de noticias visitaron el domingo el paso fronterizo terrestre, situado en un estrecho desfiladero fluvial, en un viaje organizado por el Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores de China.
No quedaba rastro alguno del edificio de aduanas chino de cinco plantas que se alzaba en la frontera antes de la catástrofe, según mostraban los vídeos y las imágenes tomadas en el lugar. La única estructura aún visible de antes del alud de lodo era una parte de una torre de agua cercana.
Los trabajadores habían colocado una bandera china en el lugar donde antes se encontraba la puerta fronteriza, de casi 20 metros de altura.
Detrás de las señales de peligro en las que se leía «Zona de peligro, pasar rápidamente», tres grupos de unos 20 trabajadores de rescate y recuperación excavaban la tierra con palas, mientras varias excavadoras permanecían a la espera el domingo por la tarde.

items.title: Dodgers turn to Justin Wrobleski in series finale vs. Nationals
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: After dealing with a number of lineup changes of late, the Los Angeles Dodgers will make an adjustment to their starting rotation in the series finale against the visiting Washington Nationals on Sunday night.
items.body:
After dealing with a number of lineup changes of late, the Los Angeles Dodgers will make an adjustment to their starting rotation in the series finale against the visiting Washington Nationals on Sunday night.
Justin Wrobleski, who was a National League All-Star this season, will make the start in his return to the rotation.
Los Angeles (85-57) has played the last three games without Shohei Ohtani, who is dealing with right biceps, neck and left knee injuries.
Dalton Rushing was expected to replace Ohtani at designated hitter on Saturday, but he was a late scratch with elbow discomfort.
Veteran Freddie Freeman received a day of rest Friday, while catcher Will Smith was used off the bench Saturday. Max Muncy was also a late scratch Saturday with an illness. Tommy Edman, Teoscar Hernandez and Mookie Betts are due for days off soon as well.
Edman proved to be the hero Saturday with a go-ahead three-run home run in the seventh inning of a 6-5 victory over the Nationals. Hernandez had an RBI single from the DH spot.
Ohtani took swings in an indoor batting cage Saturday for the first time in three days. If he goes on the IL on Sunday it will be for a minimum of 15 days, which is required of pitchers and designated two-way players.
"I think the main thing with (keeping Ohtani on the active roster) is his health," Roberts said. "That's the most important thing. And then we can find ways to log at-bats to get him up to speed. So I think that's kind of where all of our heads are at."
Wrobleski (11-5, 3.65 ERA) was bumped from the rotation last month when Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow returned from the injured list. He went on the injured list on August 16 with forearm discomfort.
He entered Tuesday's game in the seventh inning vs. St. Louis and allowed three runs (two earned) in two innings of a 13-8 loss.
Wrobleski was blitzed for eight runs on eight hits in five innings of his lone start last season against the Nationals.
James Wood had a single and a run scored for the Nationals in Saturday's defeat, the third consecutive for the club. Wood has a hit in all three games since his return from a month away because of a left oblique strain.
"When you have an extended period of time like he had injured, you worry about the timing," Nationals manager Blake Butera said, according to MLB.com. "But he's done a nice job, especially as he's gotten more at-bats since he's been back, looking comfortable all the time."
Wood has five home runs, with 12 RBIs and 10 runs scored in 11 career games against the Dodgers.
Keibert Ruiz returned for Washington on Saturday and had two hits with an RBI after last playing Wednesday when he was hit by a foul ball in his catcher's mask. Ruiz is a former Dodgers' prospect who was traded to the Nationals in 2021.
Washington (67-77) is set to send left-hander Andrew Alvarez (2-6, 3.47) to the mound. Alvarez, a native of nearby Los Alamitos, is coming off his best start of the season when he went six scoreless innings last Sunday against the Miami Marlins.
It will be Alvarez's first career start at Dodger Stadium, which is less than 30 miles north of his hometown.
-Field Level Media

items.title: Alemania planea un escudo antisabotaje tras el ataque con un dron en el aeropuerto
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Alemania está preparando un amplio paquete de medidas para reforzar sus defensas frente a ataques con drones, intrusiones cibernéticas y otras formas de sabotaje ruso tras el fallido ataque con drones perpetrado el mes pasado en un aeropuerto, declaró el domingo un portavoz del Ministerio del Interior.
items.body:
Alemania está preparando un amplio paquete de medidas para reforzar sus defensas frente a ataques con drones, intrusiones cibernéticas y otras formas de sabotaje ruso tras el fallido ataque con drones perpetrado el mes pasado en un aeropuerto, declaró el domingo un portavoz del Ministerio del Interior.
El ministro del Interior, Alexander Dobrindt, declaró al periódico "Bild am Sonntag" —que fue el primero en informar sobre estos planes— que los ataques híbridos de Rusia se habían convertido en parte de la realidad cotidiana.
"Estos ataques aumentarán, pero podemos defendernos y protegernos", afirmó Dobrindt según se cita en el artículo.
Rusia lleva mucho tiempo rechazando las acusaciones de que está llevando a cabo operaciones en Europa Occidental y ha negado su implicación en el ataque al aeropuerto alemán; el ministro de Asuntos Exteriores, Serguéi Lavrov, afirmó que las acusaciones eran "el comienzo de una guerra real", según la agencia estatal de noticias TASS.
Según el portavoz del ministerio, el plan prevé ampliar las capacidades móviles de la policía para la defensa contra drones, con unidades antidrones de despliegue rápido estacionadas en las ciudades para proteger el espacio aéreo sobre los nudos de transporte críticos y los barrios gubernamentales.
A las empresas que gestionan infraestructuras críticas, como las compañías eléctricas y los fabricantes del sector de la defensa, se les concedería la autoridad legal no solo para detectar drones, sino también para repelerlos de forma activa.
Se crearía un escudo protector nacional, o "cibercúpula", que incluiría una red de sensores digitales diseñados para detectar e interceptar intentos de ataques informáticos.
El Gobierno también tiene la intención de ampliar el uso de tecnologías basadas en la inteligencia artificial, el reconocimiento facial biométrico y la videovigilancia —por ejemplo, en las estaciones de tren— para identificar a presuntos atacantes que preparen actos de sabotaje.

items.title: South Korea's Lee Chang-dong tackles labour trauma in Venice comeback
items.author: Hanna Rantala
items.creator: Hanna Rantala
items.summary: South Korean director Lee Chang-dong returned to the big screen on Sunday after an eight-year hiatus with Venice Film Festival contender "Possible Love", revisiting a divisive labour conflict that shook his home country.
items.body:
South Korean director Lee Chang-dong returned to the big screen on Sunday after an eight-year hiatus with Venice Film Festival contender "Possible Love", revisiting a divisive labour conflict that shook his home country.
Lee's last film "Burning" was released in 2018 and he said the lengthy gap between films had allowed him to reflect on his responsibilities as a filmmaker.
"I promised that it wouldn't take another eight years, but I was unable to keep that promise," he told Reuters. "During that time, I was able to explore, more deeply and more profoundly than ever, the fundamental questions about what cinema is and what I can do through film."
VIOLENT STRIKE CRACKDOWN Inspired by real events, the film traces the consequences of mass layoffs at a major South Korean conglomerate in 2009, which sparked a prolonged strike and a violent police crackdown that left many workers traumatised.
"I thought that the incident was not a problem for one company, but an incident that sent a shockwave through the South Korean society," the director said.
Lee said he had originally planned to make a film directly about the dispute more than a decade ago and even completed a screenplay, but abandoned the project after questioning whether it was necessary to fictionalise the workers' experiences.
"There was already a great, honest and sincere documentary out there, so I wasn't sure whether I really needed to dramatise their lives to tell their story," he said.
Lee revived the project in 2024 when longtime collaborator Oh Jung-mi suggested combining the labour story with that of a fictional documentary filmmaker.
The movie follows two couples, played by Jeon Do-yeon, Sul Kyung-gu, Cho Yeo-jeong and Zo In-sung, whose lives intersect during the production of a film about the laid-off workers.
Jeon plays the wife of a former worker struggling with the fallout from the dispute, who carries the emotional weight of the family's ordeal. "But she's a passionate character with a very strong will, who tries to keep steering the family in a hopeful direction," the actor told Reuters.
Zo, who plays the wealthy husband of the documentary maker, said the film's focus on work and human dignity resonated in an age of rapid technological change.
"With the emergence of AI and the potential loss of the value of human labour, we must continue to discuss how to maintain human dignity," he said.
Venice holds special significance for Lee, whose 2002 drama "Oasis" earned him the festival's Silver Lion for best director. He said he hoped audiences would once again embrace a film that asks difficult questions.
"I hope the story shown in this film becomes an opportunity for more people to watch and understand the film, and to find their own answers to the questions the film raises," he said.
"Possible Love", which South Korea has nominated as its entry for next year's Oscars, is one of 21 movies competing for Venice's Golden Lion.

items.title: Cardinals strive to cap wild series vs. Rockies with a win
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The St. Louis Cardinals are more than halfway through their nine-game road trip, and it hasn't been boring.
items.body:
The St. Louis Cardinals are more than halfway through their nine-game road trip, and it hasn't been boring.
The Cardinals took two of three against the Los Angeles Dodgers, missing a sweep by one pitch, and then rallied to win 7-6 on Friday night in the opener against the Colorado Rockies.
After Saturday's 10-7 loss dropped the Cardinals to 3-2 on the trip, they'll vie for a series win over the Rockies on Sunday afternoon when the teams reconvene in Denver.
St. Louis' Kyle Leahy (10-4, 3.13 ERA) will match up with Colorado's Tanner Gordon (1-4, 5.18) in a battle of right-handers.
Leahy, who grew up near Denver, is 2-0 with a 4.05 ERA in six appearances (one start) against his hometown team.
The Cardinals (71-72) are on the fringe of the National League wild-card race. They are four games behind the Arizona Diamondbacks, who sit in the third and final spot.
The most dramatic win came Friday night when Ivan Herrera hit a three-run homer in the ninth inning to turn a 6-4 deficit into a 7-6 victory, and it came after manager Oliver Marmol was ejected in the sixth.
Marmol stood up for his pitcher, Hancel Rincon, who made his major league debut, after home plate umpire Doug Eddings directed the rookie to straighten his cap.
"He took it upon himself to tell our rookie pitcher the kid's 'not going to wear his hat on my field that way,'" Marmol said. "You got Dontrelle Willis, CC Sabathia, Pedro Strop -- plenty of guys that have worn it way more tilted. I have an issue with that. That's just a power-hungry move, in my opinion."
The Rockies (55-87) are trying to finish with a winning record on their six-game homestand.
Despite having the worst record in the NL, they have generated excitement. Colorado has surpassed last season's win total (43) and holds a 17-22 record in one-run games.
"I was doing some reflection and was very curious to see how many games we've lost by one or two runs -- that number is 43," outfielder Mickey Moniak said. "That's not counting the three-run, four-run, even five-run games we felt we were in. But if you look back to last year, we lost 119 games, and I'd be very curious to see how many of those were by two or fewer runs, and I would venture to say not a lot of them."
There has been a slew of close games for the Rockies over the last week -- seven in a row were decided by one or two runs before Saturday night.
Gordon was on the mound for the last comfortable win, a 13-1 victory at Washington on Aug. 26. He is facing St. Louis for the second time this season. He took the loss after allowing two runs in 3 1/3 innings at Busch Stadium on Aug. 9.
Overall, he is 1-1 with a 1.93 ERA against the Cardinals in three appearances (one start).
--Field Level Media

items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Six people have been rescued after a building collapsed in the Indian capital Delhi, news agency ANI reported on Sunday, citing the police.
items.body:
Six people have been rescued after a building collapsed in the Indian capital Delhi, news agency ANI reported on Sunday, citing the police.
It was not immediately clear how many people were inside the premises at the time of the incident.
Located in South-West Delhi, the building was being used as guest accommodation and comprised a basement along with five upper floors. According to the report, repair work was underway in the basement when the structure collapsed.
"All agencies are working in coordination, with every effort focused on the safe rescue," Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said in a post on X.
Delhi Police did not immediately respond to a Reuters' request for comment.

items.title: Spencer Jones, Yankees aim for series win against his hometown Padres
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The Spencer Jones homecoming tour continues to play to rave reviews in San Diego.
items.body:
The Spencer Jones homecoming tour continues to play to rave reviews in San Diego.
The New York Yankees' rookie outfielder kick-started a four-run second inning rally Saturday with an RBI double that helped his team post a 5-1 road win. Jones and his teammates will shoot for a series win on Sunday in the finale of a six-game road trip.
Jones, a product of nearby Encinitas, put New York up 2-1 in the 10th inning Friday night with an RBI single against Padres closer Mason Miller. But his hero turn was canceled when Luis Campusano blasted a game-winning two-run homer in the bottom of the inning.
Nevertheless, Jones is providing quality at-bats while moving to center field on a temporary basis. The Yankees put Trent Grisham on the injured list earlier Saturday with a hamstring injury he suffered in the second inning on Friday night.
"Obviously, I'm super-happy with the Yankees and being here with this organization," Jones said after Friday night's game. "But San Diego is where I grew up and my hometown, so it was really cool."
Manager Aaron Boone says Jones' defense has room for improvement but is obviously comfortable enough with his skill set to play him there.
"Overall, he's done a good job," Boone said.
So has New York pitching in the series. It allowed only three hits in Saturday's win, improving the team's record to 81-61 and enabling it to stay within four games of Tampa Bay in the American League East. The Yankees also maintained their 3 1/2-game lead over Boston for the AL's first wild-card spot.
They'll send Gerrit Cole (8-7, 3.29) to the mound on Sunday. He's coming off a 7-3 win Tuesday night at the Los Angeles Angels, which touched him for eight hits and three runs over 5 1/3 innings with a walk and five strikeouts. Cole is 5-2 with a 2.36 ERA in eight career starts against San Diego.
Cole will face former teammate Michael King (9-9, 3.11), who worked six shutout innings Monday night in a 5-0 win at Cincinnati. King yielded four hits and three walks, striking out six. He's faced New York just once since it traded him to the Padres in December 2023, allowing two runs in six innings last year during a no-decision.
San Diego (74-68) dropped a half-game behind Arizona, a 4-3 winner in 10 innings Saturday night at Houston, for the National League's last wild-card spot. The Padres have lost eight of their last 11 games since sweeping Minnesota two weekends ago, enabling the Diamondbacks to run them down.
For right fielder Fernando Tatis Jr., it's no big secret what San Diego must do to earn its fifth playoff berth in seven years.
"If we want to gain momentum, we just got to win more games," he said.
Saturday's game was just another example, according to manager Craig Stammen, about how the momentum it's claimed teams get with a big win can be quashed just hours later.
"The walkoff from (Friday) is already forgotten for both teams," he said. "Just a tough second inning turns the tides of that game."
--Field Level Media

items.title: White Sox reset rotation, ask bullpen to pull out win vs. Twins
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The Chicago White Sox know that opting for a bullpen game during a playoff hunt is less than ideal.
items.body:
The Chicago White Sox know that opting for a bullpen game during a playoff hunt is less than ideal.
But Chicago is more focused on the next couple of weeks than the next 24 hours. The White Sox will lean on their relievers in the rubber match of a three-game series against the visiting Minnesota Twins on Sunday.
White Sox right-hander Sean Burke initially was slated to start the series finale. But those plans changed after manager Will Venable and his coaching staff looked at the upcoming schedule and saw an opportunity to reset their rotation.
Chicago (74-68) has an off day Monday, and the White Sox coaches decided to scratch Burke's Sunday start and give him an additional day off Monday. That means he is set to take the mound on extra rest Tuesday in the opener of a three-game home series against the Pittsburgh Pirates, and the rest of the rotation will get more rest, too.
"(We) have a chance to line some things up," Venable said. "We're looking ahead and trying to get guys in the best spots. There's some implications with rest. There's some implications with matchups."
Part of the reason for the change is that Burke is well past his career high in innings. In 28 games (24 starts) this season, he's at 154 2/3 innings. In 2025, he appeared in 28 games (22 starts) and threw 134 1/3.
"We've seen him so good," Venable said. "(I) feel like he's getting back to form after a couple (outings) that maybe weren't as sharp as the previous stretch. Feel really good about where he's at and want to make sure that he stays there."
In Burke's place, White Sox left-handed reliever Bryan Hudson (4-4, 3.03 ERA) will serve as the opener. He has 55 strikeouts in 59 1/3 innings this season spread over 61 games.
Hudson is no stranger to facing the Twins. He has squared off against them in seven career relief appearances, and he is 0-0 with a 1.23 ERA in those outings. He has walked one and struck out five in 7 1/3 innings and tallied two saves.
Five of those appearances against the Twins have come this season in relief. He has thrown five scoreless innings, giving up four hits and striking out three, and converted both of his save opportunities.
The Twins (68-74) will counter with right-hander Bailey Ober (7-4, 4.37), who is set to make his 22nd start of the season. He is searching for his first win since July 17 against the Chicago Cubs.
Ober's most recent outing came against the White Sox on Aug. 29. He drew a no-decision in a 3-2 loss after giving up two runs (one earned) on two hits in five innings. He walked two and struck out five.
In 16 career starts against the White Sox, Ober is 6-2 with a 3.56 ERA.
Minnesota is clinging to faint hopes of a wild-card playoff berth and also looking to get its starting rotation in order for the next few weeks. The Twins hope to welcome back ace right-hander Joe Ryan as early as Monday against the Detroit Tigers.
Ryan was put on the 15-day injured list on Aug. 7 due to a left glute strain.
"We know how talented (Ryan) is," catcher Ryan Jeffers said. "He's a two-time All-Star, back-to-back years. He's the ring leader of that starting pitching group.
"Adding him back when every game feels like it's a super important game, if we can get a couple starts from him going down the stretch, then we like our chances there."
The teams will conclude the season series on Sunday, with the White Sox leading 7-5. Chicago enters the day with a 2 1/2-game lead over the Cleveland Guardians in the American League Central division. The Twins are 3 1/2 games out of the final wild-card spot.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Blue Jays push their way into wild-card spot, seek to sweep Royals
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The Toronto Blue Jays are getting hot at the right time -- and taking advantage of the struggling Kansas City Royals in the process.
items.body:
The Toronto Blue Jays are getting hot at the right time -- and taking advantage of the struggling Kansas City Royals in the process.
Aiming for a season-high fifth straight victory, the visiting Blue Jays will look to complete a three-game series sweep of the Royals on Sunday.
Toronto (72-71) lost two of three to Kansas City (63-80) from Aug. 25-27, but is 7-1 since then. After winning 9-2 over the Royals on Friday, the Blue Jays got four hits from Kazuma Okamoto, including a tie-breaking RBI single in the seventh inning, for a 4-3 victory on Saturday.
The Blue Jays are above .500 for the first time since 4-3 on April 3 and will enter play Sunday tied for the final American League wild-card spot.
"We're a really good baseball team," infielder Ernie Clement told the Blue Jays' official website.
"It was only a matter of time before things started clicking and we started playing our game."
Toronto now will try to sweep its second road series of the season. They last accomplished the feat June 16-18 at Fenway Park against the Boston Red Sox.
"It's nice to win," Blue Jays manager John Schneider said. "It's nice to get on a little bit of a roll.
"It's nice to be in this position, for sure."
Okamoto is 7-for-20 with three extra-base hits and four RBIs in his past five games. Meanwhile, teammate Nathan Lukes is 8-for-19 with four RBIs in the past four contests.
Right-hander Spencer Arrighetti (7-8, 4.82 ERA) is the scheduled starter.
He has made three appearances (one start) for Toronto since he was acquired from the Houston Astros at the trade deadline. Arrighetti's most recent start came Aug. 27 against the Royals, when he yielded four runs - three earned - and five hits, with two walks, over four innings of Toronto's 13-2 loss.
Arrighetti yielded a two-run homer and one other hit over 3 2/3 innings as the Blue Jays' third pitcher of the game at Cleveland on Tuesday.
"You need Spencer Arrighetti to go quite a bit," Schneider said.
With the Blue Jays, Arrighetti has an 0-3 record with a 6.55 ERA.
Kansas City stars Bobby Witt Jr., Jac Caglianone and Carter Jensen are a combined 8-for-16 against Arrighetti.
Caglianone is questionable for the game. He left Saturday's game in the top of the third inning with elbow soreness.
"We'll get it checked out (Sunday) morning," Royals manager Matt Quatraro said of Caglianone, the AL Player of the Month for August, when he batted .411 with six homers and 26 RBIs.
Witt had three hits against the Blue Jays last week, but he's batting .194 in eight games since for Kansas City, who are 1-5 after winning 12 of the previous 13.
Scheduled Royals starter Randy Dobnak (2-3, 2.65) will look to rebound after he allowed a season-high six runs and seven hits, including two homers, over six innings of a 6-3 loss to Miami on Tuesday.
That performance came after the right-hander gave up a three-run homer to Lukes, and five other hits, over six innings of Kansas City's 3-0 loss at Toronto on Aug. 26.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Italian Grand Prix re-started after Leclerc crashes out
items.author: Alan Baldwin
items.creator: Alan Baldwin
items.summary: The Italian Formula One Grand Prix was halted and then restarted after Ferrari's Charles Leclerc crashed heavily at Parabolica at the end of the second lap on Sunday.
items.body:
The Italian Formula One Grand Prix was halted and then restarted after Ferrari's Charles Leclerc crashed heavily at Parabolica at the end of the second lap on Sunday.
Ferrari reported the Monegasque was OK after a trip to the Monza medical centre.
Leclerc had extracted himself from the car and sat hunched on the grass behind the barriers in the immediate aftermath.
The field lined up again after a half-hour wait for the tyre wall to be rebuilt, with Mercedes' George Russell leading.
Leclerc had started the race in third place with teammate Lewis Hamilton alongside in fourth but the Briton tried to pass down the inside at the first corner, with the seven-time world champion forced wide into the gravel and plunging to 11th place.
"Charles pushed me off," Hamilton complained over the radio, in an incident noted by stewards, before the home race -- in front of a record crowd at Monza -- suddenly turned into even more of a nightmare.
Television replays showed Leclerc, in fourth place but under pressure from McLaren's Oscar Piastri, had suffered wheelspin, touched the white line at the edge of the track and skewed off at speed at the end of lap two.
The safety car was deployed and then the red flags came out on lap four.
The initial restart had to be aborted when Racing Bulls' stand-in Yuki Tsunoda was out of place on the grid.

items.title: Rangers hope to stay in playoff hunt in series finale vs. Rays
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The Texas Rangers are beginning to see their playoff hopes drift away.
items.body:
The Texas Rangers are beginning to see their playoff hopes drift away.
They'll try to start reeling them back in when they host the Tampa Bay Rays in the finale of their four-game series on Sunday afternoon in Arlington, Texas.
The Rangers (70-73) have lost two in a row and three of four since pulling within a half game of the final wild-card spot in the American League.
Texas will head into Sunday two games back of the Cleveland Guardians and Toronto Blue Jays for the final wild-card berth and three games back of the Houston Astros atop the AL West.
"We're going to do whatever we can to try and get this right because time's running out here," Rangers manager Skip Schumaker said following a 6-3, 10-inning loss to the Rays on Saturday. "We've got to start collecting some wins because we're digging ourselves a little bit of a hole right now."
The Rangers identified Junior Caminero and Jonathan Aranda as players to stop heading into the series, but they've come up short the past two games.
Caminero is 4-for-10 with a double, home run and three RBIs, and Aranda is 4-for-9 with two home runs and five RBIs.
"Caminero and Aranda have done some damage against us and we've got to make sure they're not beating us," Schumaker said. "We've got to take a look at exactly what we're doing wrong because they've been slugging and doing damage in the wrong time of the game."
Aranda has four home runs overall in the past 11 games after hitting just one in the first 34 games following the All-Star break.
"The home runs will come," Aranda said through an interpreter after hitting a three-run homer in the 10th inning of Saturday's win. "I'll take them whenever they do, but I'm a contact hitter first and foremost. So, just being able to feel myself in the box, feeling comfortable and being able to put the ball in play, is the big thing."
The Rays (85-57) will try to find some run support for Ian Seymour when he takes the mound on Sunday.
Seymour (9-6, 4.21 ERA) has lost his past three starts, but didn't pitch poorly in any of them as the offense scored just two runs while he was in those games.
He most recently allowed three runs over 6 1/3 innings in a 3-2 loss to the New York Mets on Monday, going without walking a batter for the second straight outing, and striking out 10.
Seymour has faced the Rangers just once in his career. He threw 4 2/3 innings of scoreless relief on July 29 to earn the win in the 3-0 victory. He won his next two outings as well, both starts, before beginning his current winless streak.
MacKenzie Gore is penciled in to start for the Rangers on Sunday.
Gore (8-10, 4.31) beat the Athletics his last time out. The left-hander held them to one run and five hits in 5 1/3 innings of the 8-5 win.
Gore made his only career appearance against the Rays in that July 29 matchup, going seven innings as the starter and taking the loss after allowing all three runs. He allowed first inning home runs to Yandy Diaz and Ryan Vilade.
-Field Level Media

items.title: El presidente Infantino se presentará a la reelección en marzo: FIFA
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: El presidente de la FIFA, Gianni Infantino, sigue decidido a presentarse a la reelección a pesar de la renovada oposición a su candidatura tras un plan fallido para vender una participación en las competiciones de la FIFA a inversionistas privados, según declaró el domingo un portavoz del organismo mundial del fútbol.
items.body:
El presidente de la FIFA, Gianni Infantino, sigue decidido a presentarse a la reelección a pesar de la renovada oposición a su candidatura tras un plan fallido para vender una participación en las competiciones de la FIFA a inversionistas privados, según declaró el domingo un portavoz del organismo mundial del fútbol.
Infantino, que ya había anunciado que se presentaría a un cuarto mandato en marzo del año que viene, se ha enfrentado a peticiones de dimisión por parte de la UEFA, la AFC y la CONCACAF, después de que su plan de vender una participación del 20 % en el Mundial y otros eventos de la FIFA fuera descartado en julio ante la amplia reacción negativa que suscitó.
No obstante, el presidente, de 56 años, sigue contando con el apoyo de las confederaciones africana y sudamericana.
"El presidente de la FIFA anunció en abril que se presentará a la reelección en 2027. Por supuesto, nada ha cambiado. El señor Infantino se presentará a la reelección", declaró un portavoz de la FIFA en un comunicado.
El comunicado se publicó después de que Infantino se mantuviera hermético cuando se le preguntó si se arrepentía de las turbulentas últimas seis semanas, mientras asistía el sábado al Mundial Sub-20 en Polonia.
"Habrá mucho que decir, pero habrá un lugar y un momento adecuados para hacerlo", había dicho Infantino.
Nadie ha anunciado oficialmente su candidatura para disputarle el puesto a Infantino en las elecciones del año que viene.

items.title: Nepali woman found alive days after family began mourning rites
items.author: Adnan Abidi
items.creator: Adnan Abidi
items.summary: Despite the devastation of the floods, rescuers have found people who survived extraordinary conditions, including Chandika Kumari Shrestha who survived in a narrow pocket of air in her collapsed home.
items.body:
Believing she had perished in Nepal's [USN:L1N44W056 TEXT:"deadly floods"], the family of Chandika Kumari Shrestha started the ritual of mourning the elderly woman's death.
Ten days later, rescuers found her alive inside her collapsed home in the devastated Betrawati village, where she had survived in a narrow pocket of air amid water and mud.
"The four-storey house was swept (away) by the floods and the house was left in the middle of a quicksand. While walking around it, we heard a voice 'save me,'" police officer Mahendra Darnal said.
In a rescue operation on Saturday lasting 45 minutes, Darnal and his team found Shrestha in a confined space and sent her to an army hospital.
"I was in touch with the family and they had started the 11-day mourning period," Darnal said.
Shrestha was among the hundreds missing in Betrawati, an area among the hardest hit by the floods in Nepal and engulfed with white deposits compacted almost like concrete. Crews continue to recover scores of dead bodies.
The town's market and most residential buildings, some as tall as four storeys, were almost completely buried under debris left by a torrent that swept through the valley, part of a disaster that killed more than 1,300 people across Nepal. Thousands remain unaccounted for.
Rescue workers wearing hard hats were seen digging with shovels, while some were crawling through the gaps of collapsed buildings periodically blowing whistles to get the attention of anyone trapped and alive.
Five days earlier, 24 bodies were found in a decomposed state in Betrawati's market area in a building that had contained a small shop, Darnal said.
LOOKING FOR SIGNS OF LIFE Eleven days since a glacial collapse triggered the devastating floods, close to 5,000 are still missing.
Hundreds of bodies have been swept onto the banks of rivers far from the ravaged Rasuwa district. In Chitwan, hundreds of miles away, several rounds of [USN:L1N44R01F TEXT:"mass burials"] have taken place for unidentified and badly decomposed bodies.
Even as hope is beginning to fade, Nepal authorities continue their effort to look for people stuck in tunnels and under the thick deposits of mud that have hardened over buildings.
Since Friday, they have pulled out [USN:L1N44W056 TEXT:"three people from the tunnels"], including a [USN:L4N44X01J TEXT:"Chinese citizen"] by the Trishuli river, where more than 900 are believed to be trapped.
Others like Shrestha have survived in extraordinary conditions, including an [USN:L4N44P0XH TEXT:"8-year-old boy"] who was also reunited with his mother.

items.body:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino remains committed to standing for re-election amid renewed opposition to his candidacy after [USN:L1N43X04P TEXT:"a botched plan"] to sell a stake in FIFA competitions to private investors, a spokesperson for the global soccer body said on Sunday.
Infantino, who had previously announced that he would seek a fourth term in March next year, has faced calls to resign from UEFA, the AFC and CONCACAF, after his plan to sell a 20% stake in the World Cup and other FIFA events was scrapped amid widespread backlash in July.
But the 56-year-old retains support from the African and South American confederations.
"The FIFA president announced in April that he will stand for re-election in 2027. Of course, nothing has changed. Mr Infantino will be standing for re-election," a FIFA spokesperson said in a statement.
The statement came after Infantino [USN:L1N44X02Z TEXT:"remained tight-lipped"] when asked whether he regretted the [USN:L6N44V19H TEXT:"turbulent last six weeks"] while attending the U-20 World Cup in Poland on Saturday.
"There will be a lot to say, but there will be a right place and a right time to say this," Infantino had said.
No one has formally announced a candidacy to challenge Infantino in next year's election.

items.title: Poland says suspected airspace violation caused by bird flock
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Authorities in Poland said on Sunday that a suspected violation of the country's airspace originating on the other side of its border with neighbouring Belarus had been caused by a large flock of birds.
items.body:
Authorities in Poland said on Sunday that a suspected violation of the country's airspace originating on the other side of its border with neighbouring Belarus had been caused by a large flock of birds.
The event had prompted the Polish military to scramble helicopters to verify data of a possible violation registered by radiolocation systems shortly after noon local time (1000 GMT), a spokesman for Polish Armed Forces Operational Command told Reuters.
"Indications recorded by the radar systems were not related to a violation of Polish airspace. They were caused by a large flock of birds, whose passage was recorded by airspace surveillance systems," the army later wrote on X.
Poland's air traffic authority PANSA wrote in a separate post on X that Rzeszow Airport in southeastern Poland had resumed operations after they were briefly suspended in order to facilitate military aviation.

Gulf stock markets ended mixed on Sunday, with traders treading carefully against the backdrop of an escalating standoff between Washington and Tehran.
Iran has [USN:L1N44Y02B TEXT:"pledged"] to counter crippling U.S. sanctions while threatening a "painful response" to any further aggression. Six months after initial U.S.-Israeli strikes , the conflict remains at a stalemate as diplomatic peace efforts stall following the collapse of a June ceasefire.
Meanwhile, tit-for-tat military action has resumed after a brief July lull, with U.S. Central Command confirming it struck three Iranian tankers on Saturday in retaliation for ballistic missile attacks on two U.S. Navy warships.
Saudi Arabia's benchmark index (.TASI) edged 0.3% higher, bolstered by heavyweight lenders, as Al Rajhi Bank (1120.SE) gained 0.7% and Saudi National Bank (1180.SE) climbed 1.1%.
In Qatar, the index (.QSI) lost 0.3%, hit by a 0.7% fall in Qatar Islamic Bank (QISB.QA) .

items.title: イランと米国、ホルムズ海峡でタンカー攻撃の応酬－戦争終結見通せず
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： イランは、この週末に米国がイランのタンカーを攻撃したことへの報復として、ホルムズ海峡で許可されていない航路を通航していた石油タンカー3隻のほか、米国と関係のある複数の船舶を標的にしたと明らかにした。

イスラム革命防衛隊（IRGC）海軍はこれについて一段の詳細を明らかにしておらず、5日遅くのテレグラムへの投稿でも、船舶に攻撃が命中したかどうかは明示しなかった。IRGCはその後、ホルムズ海峡に進入しようとした米海軍の無人機と米軍の無人水上艇も攻撃したと発表した。

世界のエネルギー輸送の要衝であるホルムズ海峡周辺でこうした攻撃があったことを裏付ける独立した情報は、直ちには得られていない。同海峡は米国とイランの和平合意を巡る重要な焦点となっている。

IRGCの発表に先立ち、米軍はイランの原油タンカー3隻を攻撃し、うち1隻を撃沈したと発表していた。IRGCが米海軍の艦船2隻に向けて弾道ミサイルを発射したことへの対抗措置だと説明した。

相次ぐ報復攻撃は、米国とイスラエルが6カ月余り前に開始した対イラン戦争の早期終結見通しが乏しいことを示唆している。

ペルシャ湾とオマーン湾を結ぶホルムズ海峡の通航は依然として細っている。調査会社ケプラーのデータによると、5日に同海峡を通過したと確認された商船はわずか1隻だった。

イランのガリバフ国会議長は6日、「相応の対応」の時代は終わったと警告した。同氏はこれまでの停戦協議で首席交渉官を務めた。

ガリバフ氏はテレグラムへの投稿で、米国は「手遅れになる前に、ゲームのルールが変わったことを理解しなければならない」と述べた。「今後は、イランの利益と安全保障に対するいかなる攻撃にも、より迅速かつ強力で、より痛みを伴う対応を取る」と表明した。

トランプ米大統領は、数カ月に及ぶイランとの戦争の終結に苦戦する一方、同国経済を締め上げたいとの考えを示している。4日には、この戦争について「取るに足らないことだ」と述べた。またバンス米副大統領は3日、「戦争とは呼ばない」と発言した。

items.title: Astros aim to complete busy stretch with win vs. D-backs
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The finale of their three-game interleague series with the visiting Arizona Diamondbacks on Sunday will mark the conclusion of a stretch of 13 games in 13 days for the Houston Astros.
items.body:
The finale of their three-game interleague series with the visiting Arizona Diamondbacks on Sunday will mark the conclusion of a stretch of 13 games in 13 days for the Houston Astros.
The Astros' 4-3, 10-inning loss on Saturday did not impact their position in the American League West standings, as the Texas Rangers' home loss to the Tampa Bay Rays allowed Houston to maintain its three-game lead.
Still, with a welcome day off coming on Monday, the Astros are laboring to cap this current stretch on a high note.
"We have 20 games left," Astros manager Joe Espada said. "We're going to be facing some really good teams in September; they're aware of that. So they know we can rest later. Right now, we've got to stay locked in.
"I'm so proud of the way they're playing. Once the game has started, they have been locked in and playing the game really hard."
Right-hander Peter Lambert (8-7, 3.66 ERA) is scheduled to start the series rubber match for Houston (73-70).
Lambert did not factor into the decision in a 6-3 win over the Chicago White Sox last Monday, allowing two runs on three hits and a season-high five walks with six strikeouts over 4 2/3 innings.
Since earning his eighth win on July 11 against Texas, Lambert is 0-2 with a 4.63 ERA across nine starts.
Lambert is 2-1 with a 3.79 ERA in six career appearances (two starts) against Arizona. In his previous appearance against the Diamondbacks on Aug 14, 2024, he allowed one unearned run on two hits and two walks with one strikeout over 2 1/3 innings in the Colorado Rockies' 11-4 loss.
Left-hander Eduardo Rodriguez (14-5, 2.59) has the starting assignment for Arizona (75-68) on Sunday.
Rodriguez is 5-0 with a 1.96 ERA over his last seven road starts, last losing away from home on May 15 in Colorado after allowing three runs on nine hits with six strikeouts over 5 1/3 innings. He had a four-start win streak snapped on Tuesday, allowing three runs on eight hits and three walks with three strikeouts over five innings in a 7-1 loss to the Philadelphia Phillies.
Rodriguez, who owns a career winning percentage of 60.3, is 1-7 with a 6.67 ERA in 12 career starts against the Astros. In his previous start against Houston on July 22, 2025, Rodriguez tossed 6 1/3 shutout innings, allowing six hits and three walks while striking out three. He did not factor into the decision of a 3-1 home loss.
The Diamondbacks are poised to welcome back right-handers Zac Gallen (right elbow inflammation) and Michael Soroka (right arm inflammation) from the 60-day and 15-day injured list, respectively, during the upcoming three-game interleague series at the Kansas City Royals.
Gallen and Soroka are on the same timeline, leaving the D-backs with deployment options for both. Corbin Burnes is set to rejoin the rotation Tuesday following a 15-month recovery after Tommy John surgery, so potential bullpen usage is a factor as well.
"Would we push one (back), which would give them seven days down, or do we piggyback them so they're both on the same day, which would most likely be Wednesday?" Diamondbacks manager Torey Lovullo said. "Those are the conversations we're having right now. How do we layer them back in?
"They're both gassed up and ready to go. That piggyback situation could be perfectly timed on Wednesday. Those are the important conversations we're going to have. They both feel good."
--Field Level Media

items.title: Iran's Hormuz leverage wanes as US economic squeeze bites
items.author: Samia Nakhoul
items.creator: Samia Nakhoul
items.summary: Tehran has failed to impose the costs it hoped would break Washington's resolve.
items.body:
Six months after a conflict that rattled markets and pushed the Gulf to the brink of a wider war, the tide may be turning against Iran as Washington unleashes an unprecedented economic offensive to achieve what military force could not.
After years of surviving sanctions, Tehran is now confronting one of the harshest squeezes in the Islamic Republic's history, according to Iranian insiders and regional sources. A U.S. naval blockade and [USN:L6N44T0TA TEXT:"tougher sanctions"] are curbing oil exports, restricting access to foreign currency and exposing growing strains in the economy.
The campaign has led U.S. and regional officials to wager that mounting economic pressure can force Tehran to allow free passage through the Strait of Hormuz, which carries about a fifth of global oil and LNG supplies.
Their bet rests on a simple calculation: Iran is suffering more economic damage than it is inflicting. Efforts to choke off oil exports have cut state revenues, while attempts to disrupt shipping through Hormuz have not triggered the global economic shock Tehran hoped would force Washington to compromise. Energy markets have adjusted and alternative supplies have continued to flow.
"The balance of power has tilted against Iran a bit," said Iranian analyst Arash Azizi. Iran is losing some of the leverage it had over the Strait of Hormuz because it has been unable to close it fully, he said, adding that the U.S. naval blockade was "really hitting Iran."
Azizi said Tehran had expected disruption in the strait to trigger a major shock to the global economy and drive Washington back to the negotiating table. "It hasn't happened, really," he said. Other countries had adapted, exposing limits to Iran's ability to inflict economic pain on the region and beyond.
Whether the pressure will force concessions remains unclear, the regional sources said. Tehran has failed to impose the costs it hoped would break Washington's resolve but has shown little sign of abandoning demands for sanctions relief, access to frozen assets and recognition of its security role in Hormuz.
Still, a new formula for resolving the standoff is now under discussion between mediators and Iran, the sources said.
CAN TEHRAN OUTLAST THE SQUEEZE? Three senior Iranian sources acknowledged that Washington's campaign is becoming increasingly difficult to withstand. The latest measures have sharply restricted Tehran's ability to access foreign currency, import goods and tap global financing networks that have helped keep [USN:L1N44Y02B TEXT:"the economy"] afloat.
Iranian leaders fear a worsening economy, marked by surging prices, weaker trade and pressure on household incomes, could reignite nationwide unrest that has repeatedly challenged the Islamic Republic.
Shortages of key imports, including fuel and wheat, are becoming an increasing concern, officials said.
U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent [USN:L6N44H0E8 TEXT:"described the strategy"] as a "one-two punch" combining the blockade with "the toughest sanctions in history."
"It is going to work in Iran and we are going to collapse this regime," he told CNBC.
For some U.S., Israeli and regional officials, such strains strengthen hopes that economic pressure could eventually carry political consequences inside Iran by triggering unrest, widening rifts within the leadership and weakening its grip on power.
Others remain sceptical that economic and military coercion will produce a political rupture, pointing to decades of failed efforts to destabilise the Islamic Republic and Tehran's willingness to suppress dissent. They argue Iran's rulers may again prove more resilient than their adversaries expect.
THE RESILIENCE TEST Dennis Ross, a former U.S. negotiator, said Washington may be interpreting Iran's economic distress as evidence of strategic success when the reality is more complicated. Tehran remains determined to demonstrate it can control Hormuz, but appears to be calibrating its use of force while keeping further escalation in reserve.
The Revolutionary Guards may believe Iran can absorb the economic pain and outlast the pressure rather than compromise, Ross said.
"The Iranians have consistently surprised us in terms of their resiliency," he added, saying he doubted economic and military pressure alone would force a retreat. Hardliners, he said, may believe they can endure and ultimately secure what they want.
Resilience may depend as much on public tolerance as Tehran's ability to absorb economic hardship, said Burcu Ozcelik, a senior research fellow at the Royal United Services Institute.
"Of course, the economic squeeze raises the risk of public unrest, but for now, a wartime mentality appears to have a significant hold over the population," said Ozcelik. "Foreign military intervention, civilian casualties and the perception of a wider civilization confrontation with a U.S.-led order are sustaining a degree of 'Iran-first' patriotic support, tolerance or simply patience with the regime."
The result is a more stubborn impasse than Washington may have anticipated. Economic pressure is deepening the pain, but Tehran's powerful Revolutionary Guards may see endurance, backed by the threat of escalation, as leverage rather than a reason to concede.
The key question is not whether Iran is hurting, but whether it is hurting enough to compromise before either side slips toward another confrontation, the regional sources said.
Ross said the clearest path to a deal may lie in the dispute over shipping fees through the Strait of Hormuz. Iran could abandon any demand for a toll while retaining the right to charge for legitimate navigational, security or environmental services, he said.
Such an arrangement could give both sides a claim to victory, allowing Tehran to step back without appearing to capitulate.
"If you could announce that the Strait were reopened," Ross said, "I think Trump would do a deal."
items.raw_description: Tehran has failed to impose the costs it hoped would break Washington's resolve.

items.title: Mets, Giants hope the power stays on in series finale
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: One of the biggest power outbursts of the season for the San Francisco Giants provided a glimpse at what could have been -- and what might be next season.
items.body:
One of the biggest power outbursts of the season for the San Francisco Giants provided a glimpse at what could have been -- and what might be next season.
The Giants will look to build off a homer-heavy attack that powered a 9-5 victory on Saturday as they conclude their final series in the Eastern time zone on Sunday afternoon in Queens, N.Y. against the Mets. New York won the opener 10-6 on Friday.
Giants left-hander Cesar Perdomo (0-0, 2.25 ERA) is slated to make his second big league appearance on Sunday when he starts against Mets right-hander Christian Scott (4-4, 3.80 ERA).
Scott will be tasked with keeping the ball in the ballpark.
Christian Koss and Rafael Devers both hit two homers Saturday for the Giants. Osleivis Basabe hit a two-run homer in the eighth and Grant McCray added a solo shot in the ninth for the Giants, whose six homers were one shy of their season high.
San Francisco went deep seven times on June 5 in an 18-3 rout of the Chicago Cubs, when Willy Adames, Matt Chapman and Casey Schmitt had two homers apiece and Jonah Cox homered once.
With Saturday's outburst, the Giants (59-84) have 164 homers this season, which puts them on pace for 185. San Francisco has hit at least 185 homers just once since Barry Bonds retired following the 2007 season. The 107-win 2021 squad went deep a franchise-record 241 times.
The Giants' power output has been solid despite the long-term absences of Chapman (abdomen) and Schmitt (left knee), both of whom are out for the season. Adames hasn't played since Aug. 23 due to a sprained ligament in his left elbow.
"There's some exciting names that aren't with us right now," Giants manager Tony Vitello said.
Schmitt and Adames each have 21 homers -- tied for second on the team behind Devers, whose 35 homers put him within reach of becoming the first Giants slugger with 40 homers since Bonds hit 45 homers in 2004.
The Mets (64-78) also have gotten a glimpse at a potentially brighter future in the power department during a disappointing season.
New York tied a season-high with five homers in Friday's 10-6 win. The Mets have homered at least once in each of the last six games, a span in which they have 11 homers overall.
The power surge began Aug. 30 -- one day after Juan Soto returned following a five-week stint on the injured list. Soto, Francisco Lindor and Marcus Semien, all of whom rank among the top 25 active players in career homers, have teamed up to hit 53 homers this season despite missing a combined 128 games.
In addition, National League Rookie of the Year candidate Carson Benge (16 homers, 20 stolen bases) has a chance at a 20/20 season. Fellow rookie A.J. Ewing hit a two-run homer Saturday, when he also drew a pair of walks in four plate appearances.
"I love the two walks as much as the home run," interim Mets manager Andy Green said. "I think that's indicative of him being in a good spot and trusting who he is."
Perdomo made his major league debut on Tuesday when he allowed one run over four innings of relief as the Giants fell to the Pittsburgh Pirates, 13-12. Scott last pitched Aug. 28, when he took the defeat after giving up three runs over 5 1/3 innings in the Mets' 3-1 loss to the Houston Astros.
Scott didn't factor into the decision in his lone start against the Giants on May 24, 2024, when he gave up two runs over six innings in the Mets' 8-7 loss.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Pete Crow-Armstrong, Cubs seek series sweep of Marlins
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The Chicago Cubs will look to strengthen their position atop the National League wild-card race on Sunday when they bid for a three-game sweep against the host Miami Marlins.
items.body:
The Chicago Cubs will look to strengthen their position atop the National League wild-card race on Sunday when they bid for a three-game sweep against the host Miami Marlins.
Chicago (81-62) is led by center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong, who is the current favorite to win National League Most Valuable Player Award.
Armstrong has posted career-high totals in triples (seven), homers (39) and runs (105) to go along with 28 doubles, 94 RBIs, 33 steals and a .943 OPS.
"Looking at Pete, he's the kind of player who is going to leave his mark in history," Cubs pitcher Shota Imanaga said of Armstrong, who needs one more homer to become the first Cub since Derrek Lee in 2005 to reach 40 in a season. "Having him behind me (defensively) means so much. Without Pete, we wouldn't be where we are."
The Cubs lead the majors in several offensive statistics, including runs, walks, total bases, slugging percentage, OPS and homers.
"Credit the Cubs," Marlins manager Clayton McCullough said following Saturday's 6-5 loss to Chicago. "It's a good lineup, not only with the ability to do damage but also how they work at-bats."
Aside from Armstrong, three Cubs players have hit more than 20 homers: third baseman Alex Bregman (24); right fielder Seiya Suzuki (24); and left fielder Ian Happ (23). Middle infielder Nico Hoerner, with 22 steals, gives Chicago speed along with Armstrong.
Chicago's pitching hasn't been as strong, entering the weekend ranked 17th in the majors in ERA. But acquiring Clay Holmes and David Peterson in two separate trades with the Mets have reinforced the pitching staff. The Mets also are the same franchise the Cubs used to acquire Armstrong and fellow outfielder Tyrone Taylor, who has been hot lately.
Holmes (6-6, 2.09 ERA), Sunday's expected starter, scattered five hits over six scoreless innings in a 17-3 win over the Milwaukee Brewers last Monday.
He is 3-1 with a 3.19 ERA in 13 career appearances (four starts) versus Miami.
Meanwhile, the Marlins (71-72) are in contention but currently four games outside of a wild-card playoff berth.
Miami will start right-hander Tyler Phillips (4-6, 3.43). Phillips, 28, has pitched just one inning against the Cubs, allowing two hits and no runs on May 21, 2025.
For his career, Phillips is much better as a reliever (2.49 ERA in 71 appearances) than as a starter (5.12 ERA in 24 games).
On the positive side for Phillips, he has a better career ERA at home (2.83) than on the road (4.86).
Miami's bullpen is a bit thin due to injuries to closer Pete Fairbanks and set-up man Anthony Bender.
In addition, second baseman Xavier Edwards is out due to a thumb injury.
But players such as Griffin Conine and Kyle Stowers -- who both homered on Saturday -- have stepped up for Miami. Conine has been an especially good story as he is finally shedding his injuries.
"Griffin has earned the opportunities he's getting," McCullough said. "His at-bat quality is getting better. I'm not surprised with his power (15 homers in 75 games)."
--Field Level Media

items.title: La OPEP+ mantiene sin cambios su política de producción de petróleo para octubre
items.author: Ahmad Ghaddar, Olesya Astakhova, Alex Lawler
items.creator: Ahmad Ghaddar, Olesya Astakhova, Alex Lawler
items.summary: La OPEP+ mantuvo sin cambios su política de producción de petróleo para octubre en una reunión celebrada el domingo, según indicó en un comunicado, ya que el grupo de productores debe acordar nuevas cuotas antes de decidir sus próximos pasos en materia de producción.
items.body:
La OPEP+ mantuvo sin cambios su política de producción de petróleo para octubre en una reunión celebrada el domingo, según indicó en un comunicado, ya que el grupo de productores debe acordar nuevas cuotas antes de decidir sus próximos pasos en materia de producción.
La reunión de los siete miembros principales de la OPEP+ —Arabia Saudita, Rusia, Irak, Kuwait, Argelia, Kazajistán y Omán— se produce mientras la guerra en Irán sigue perturbando las exportaciones de petróleo a través del estrecho de Ormuz, lo que limita la influencia de la OPEP+ sobre los precios y la cuota de mercado.
En agosto, la OPEP+ acordó el aumento de la producción para septiembre, completando así la retirada gradual del recorte de suministro de 1,65 millones de barriles diarios acordado inicialmente en 2023. A pesar de los aumentos de producción acordados, el grupo formado por la Organización de Países Exportadores de Petróleo y sus aliados, entre ellos Rusia, sigue produciendo muy por debajo de sus objetivos debido a la guerra.
EL PODER DE LA OPEP, LIMITADO POR EL CONFLICTO CON IRÁN «La OPEP+ tiene actualmente un poder muy limitado sobre el mercado físico del petróleo», afirmó Jorge León, de Rystad Energy. «El grupo puede modificar los objetivos de producción sobre el papel, pero no puede garantizar que esos barriles se produzcan o lleguen realmente al mercado».
«La atención se aleja ahora de los ajustes mensuales de producción y se centra en el debate, mucho más trascendental, sobre 2027».
La OPEP+ sigue aplicando otra ronda de recortes de producción, que afecta a la mayoría de los miembros del grupo de 21 países hasta finales de 2026. Antes de que el grupo decida cómo retirar los recortes y devolver la producción al mercado, debe revisar la capacidad de producción de petróleo de sus miembros para establecer las bases de referencia de producción para 2027, que constituyen la base de las cuotas.
Es probable que este debate tenga lugar a finales de 2026 y, por lo tanto, es probable que la OPEP+ suspenda sus aumentos de producción durante el cuarto trimestre, según informaron anteriormente fuentes a Reuters. La declaración del domingo no hizo mención alguna a la política más allá de octubre.
Solo los siete miembros de la OPEP+ que se reunieron el domingo, más los Emiratos Árabes Unidos hasta que abandonaron la OPEP en mayo, han participado en las decisiones mensuales sobre la producción en los últimos años.
Estos siete países celebrarán su próxima reunión el 4 de octubre.

items.title: At least 25 killed in bus crash on Cape Verde's Fogo island, agency says
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: At least 25 people, many of them schoolchildren and teenagers, were killed when a bus plunged into a ravine on Fogo, one of Cape Verde's islands in the Atlantic Ocean off the coast of West Africa, national news agency Inforpress reported on Sunday.
items.body:
At least 25 people, many of them schoolchildren and teenagers, were killed when a bus plunged into a ravine on Fogo, one of Cape Verde's islands in the Atlantic Ocean off the coast of West Africa, national news agency Inforpress reported on Sunday.
The crash occurred on a mountain road in northern Fogo late on Saturday, when the bus veered off the road and plunged about 30 metres into a steep ravine, it said.
Many of those on board were primary and secondary school students, the agency said.
Several injured passengers were taken to Sao Francisco de Assis Regional Hospital on Fogo.
Education officials said the outing was not organised by local schools but was an annual trip privately arranged by the driver, who was among those killed, Inforpress said.

items.title: Tigers look for parting shot at Guardians in finale of season series
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The high point of the Detroit Tigers' season came against the Cleveland Guardians on Aug. 13, when they moved into a share of an American League wild-card spot with a home win.
items.body:
The high point of the Detroit Tigers' season came against the Cleveland Guardians on Aug. 13, when they moved into a share of an American League wild-card spot with a home win.
Their low point did, as well, as Cleveland's two walk-off wins in a doubleheader sweep Friday essentially knocked the Tigers out of the postseason hunt.
Detroit gets its final shot at the Guardians this year on Sunday afternoon, when the teams wrap up a four-game series in Cleveland.
Tigers right-hander Jackson Jobe (1-2, 4.63 ERA) will get the start against Guardians righty Gavin Williams (13-7, 3.81).
Three-time All-Star Riley Greene gave the visitors a bit of payback on Saturday, amassing a career-high tying four hits, four RBIs, three runs and two homers in leading Detroit to a 6-0 rout of Cleveland.
It was the ninth multi-homer game of his five-year career and his first blasts anywhere since spending 20 days on the injured list with a strained right hamstring. Greene's seven home runs in Cleveland are his most in any visiting ballpark.
"We come here all the time, so maybe that's the reason why," Greene said, laughing. "It's baseball. It happens. After what happened last night, you just have to flush it and get to the next day."
The Guardians (72-71) are now even with the Toronto Blue Jays in the battle for the final AL wild-card position, but Cleveland loses the head-to-head tiebreaker. Detroit (65-77) is 6 1/2 games behind them with 20 to play.
Greene had been 1-for-13 since being activated, but came to life against his offseason buddy, Guardians All-Star pitcher Parker Messick. The homers totaled 828 feet and each landed atop the high wall in left-center field.
"I think he owes me a fishing trip that we've been talking about the last few times I've seen him," Messick quipped. "To go backside, left-center field is just a really good swing. I throw those balls there to a lot of other lefties and don't get that same result."
There won't be any hard feelings the next time they hang out in Florida, though. Greene said it didn't matter who he was hitting against, he was desperate to get back in a groove.
"I just had to get good pitches to hit and was trying to get on strikes," Greene said. "On the first one, I was just trying to find barrels and make something happen."
Jobe has either been terrific or terrible in five starts, all coming since Aug. 8 as the Tigers have fallen apart. Three of them have seen him allow one or fewer runs, but he was rocked for 10 earned runs in 8 2/3 combined innings during the other two.
His only career game against the Guardians was a home loss on May 23, 2025, when he gave up two runs in five innings.
Greene's big night coincided with Framber Valdez and two relievers tossing a three-hitter. Angel Martinez, David Fry and Angel Genao each had a single as Cleveland was shut out for the 15th time, tied for the most in the majors with the Cincinnati Reds and Pittsburgh Pirates.
"That's the most four-seam (fastballs Valdez has) used, almost 20%," Guardians manager Stephen Vogt said. "That's not something he historically does. The two fastballs, and he threw just enough off-speed, to keep us off of that."
Williams last pitched on Sept. 1, holding Toronto without an earned run in seven innings of a 6-1 victory. It was one of four wins by Cleveland in nine games on its homestand that ends Sunday.
Nicknamed "The Big Rig," Williams has not faced Detroit this season. He is 3-2 with a 1.88 ERA in seven career starts against the Central Division rival.
"We capitalized (Friday) night, right? Then today, we got beat by a very good pitcher," Vogt said. "That was the story, and we'll be ready Sunday."
--Field Level Media

items.title: Irán abordará problemas económicos y advierte de que los nuevos ataques serán "más dolorosos"
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Irán ha afirmado que intensificará sus esfuerzos para hacer frente a los problemas provocados por las sanciones estadounidenses que están paralizando su economía, mientras que un alto cargo iraní ha advertido de una "respuesta dolorosa" si el país sufre nuevos ataques.
items.body:
Irán ha afirmado que intensificará sus esfuerzos para hacer frente a los problemas provocados por las sanciones estadounidenses que están paralizando su economía, mientras que un alto cargo iraní ha advertido de una "respuesta dolorosa" si el país sufre nuevos ataques.
Seis meses después de los ataques de Estados Unidos e Israel contra Irán, la guerra parece estar en un punto muerto. El acuerdo preliminar de alto el fuego alcanzado en junio se ha desmoronado y se han logrado pocos avances en los esfuerzos diplomáticos para volver a encarrilar el proceso de paz.
Tras una pausa en las acciones militares durante gran parte de agosto, se han reanudado los ataques de represalia: el Mando Central de Estados Unidos ha afirmado que el sábado atacó tres petroleros iraníes en respuesta al lanzamiento de misiles balísticos por parte del Cuerpo de la Guardia Revolucionaria Islámica de Irán contra dos buques de la Armada de Estados Unidos.
Tras los ataques, el presidente del Parlamento iraní, Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf, declaró el domingo que Estados Unidos debería comprender que las reglas del juego en la guerra contra Irán han cambiado "antes de que sea demasiado tarde".
"A partir de ahora, cualquier ataque contra los intereses y la seguridad de Irán recibirá una respuesta más rápida, más contundente y más dolorosa", afirmó en un discurso publicado en su canal de Telegram.
Teherán ha demostrado que sigue conservando la capacidad de atacar los intereses estadounidenses en los países vecinos y de bloquear el flujo de petróleo a través del estrecho de Ormuz, por donde circulaba una quinta parte del suministro mundial de petróleo antes del conflicto.
SANCIONES Y EL BLOQUEO PETROLÍFERO ASFIXIAN LA ECONOMÍA Sin embargo, la campaña de Estados Unidos para estrangular la economía iraní mediante el bloqueo de sus exportaciones de petróleo y la lucha contra la elusión de sanciones resulta cada vez más difícil de soportar, según han afirmado tres fuentes iraníes de alto rango.
En su discurso del domingo, Qalibaf añadió que, junto al frente militar, la principal batalla de Irán se libraba ahora en torno a la producción y los medios de subsistencia de la población.
Mencionó las fuertes fluctuaciones monetarias, la inflación, el desempleo y la gestión del mercado como retos principales, y añadió que los iraníes podían tolerar las penurias, pero no la mala gestión ni la inacción, y esperaban que el Gobierno actuara con rapidez.
El ministro de Economía de Irán, Ali Madanizadeh, afirmó que Teherán tenía previsto responder a la presión económica de Estados Unidos con reformas y rechazó la idea de que las sanciones le hicieran cambiar de rumbo, según informaron el domingo los medios estatales.
"Hablan de presión económica y aislamiento, de romper los lazos financieros, y creen que, al ejercer presión sobre la economía de un país, pueden cambiar las decisiones de su pueblo", afirmó Madanizadeh.
"Tengo que aclarar un punto: la responsabilidad de reformar la economía de Irán recae en su Gobierno y su pueblo, no en el Tesoro de Estados Unidos".
Por otra parte, el viceministro de Economía, Morteza Zamanian, declaró el domingo que el "Cuartel General de la Guerra Económica" del ministerio estaba redoblando sus esfuerzos para resolver los problemas causados por la guerra, según la agencia de noticias semioficial Tasnim.
ISLA DE KHARG HA SUFRIDO 550 ATAQUES EN LOS ÚLTIMOS MESES, SEGÚN IRÁN Irán es el tercer mayor productor de la Organización de Países Exportadores de Petróleo y, antes de la guerra, exportaba el 90 % de su crudo a través de su centro de exportación de la isla de Kharg. Los flujos se han visto interrumpidos desde que, a mediados de abril, comenzó el bloqueo estadounidense a las exportaciones de petróleo iraní.
El 31 de agosto, Trump publicó un mensaje de una sola línea en las redes sociales acompañado de un vídeo generado por IA en el que se veía cómo la isla de Kharg "volaba en mil pedazos". Las autoridades iraníes han prometido una respuesta contundente si Kharg es atacada.
En una entrevista emitida el domingo en la televisión estatal, el ministro de Petróleo de Irán, Mohsen Paknejad, afirmó que la isla había sido alcanzada unas 550 veces en los meses anteriores, pero que seguía en funcionamiento.
Irán también ha impuesto un bloqueo en el estrecho de Ormuz, lo que supone un problema para el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, al provocar un aumento de los precios del combustible a nivel mundial de cara a las elecciones de mitad de mandato de su Partido Republicano en noviembre.
El sábado, el Mando Central de Estados Unidos afirmó que había atacado tres buques iraníes, incluido uno frente a la costa de la isla de Kharg, después de que el Cuerpo de la Guardia Revolucionaria Islámica de Irán lanzara misiles balísticos contra dos buques de la Armada de Estados Unidos.
"Que el mensaje al IRGC quede claro: si disparan contra dos de nuestros buques, os impondremos un coste económico aún mayor: derribaremos tres de los vuestros", afirmó el almirante Brad Cooper, jefe del Mando Central de Estados Unidos, que supervisa las fuerzas armadas estadounidenses en Oriente Medio.
